question.text: What is the process called when previously issued paper share certificates are converted into electronic form?

explanation.text: The Logic: Dematerialisation is the process of converting physical share certificates into electronic form. Since the mid-1990s, securities in India are issued in electronic form. Previously issued share certificates were also converted into electronic form by issuers through this process. The Trap: Rematerialisation (option B) is the opposite -- converting electronic holdings back to physical certificates. Securitisation (option C) is the process of converting financial assets into tradable securities. Capitalisation (option D) refers to converting reserves into share capital. Cross-Exam Context: Foundation topic tested across 22 NISM exams. Dematerialisation is covered in NISM VI (Depository Operations), V-A (Mutual Fund), and XII. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Since 2019, SEBI has made it mandatory for transfer of securities only in dematerialised form for listed companies. Always advise clients to open a demat account before investing.
